paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take from this one, friend. Solomon builds the most beautiful house, and then he stands up and says, "The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built." (2 Chronicles 6:18) The house was never the point. God is bigger than any building, and still He chooses to listen to the people who pray toward Him.

And look at how many times Solomon asks God to "hear from heaven." (2 Chronicles 6:21) Sin against a neighbor, a defeat, no rain, a plague, a war, even captivity in a faraway land. Every time, the pattern is the same: they pray, they turn back, and Solomon asks God to hear and forgive. He even says there's no one who does not sin (2 Chronicles 6:36), so if you've messed up, you're in good company, and that includes a certain stamper.

So here's the Big Idea. God is too big for any box, and He still opens His ears to you, wherever you are. Even the foreigner from a distant land gets a place in this prayer (2 Chronicles 6:32-33), so nobody is too far away to pray. When you've wandered off or blown it, you can come back and talk to Him, because He has promised to listen.
